column1: # <class><TAB><ERE every differing key matches><TAB><ERE over the command><TAB><reason>
# The first line whose two expressions both match names a mismatch. A class
# names a place where the reference itself is wrong or outside the stage, never
# a place where the core is.
# No class is open. The first one, guard-crash, named a defect of the bash
# guard that this comparison found: in safedeps_manager_long_option,
# `first="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"` read an array element that is unset when the
# option stands before the command, and under `set -u` bash ended the guard
# there (`pip --cache x install evil==1.0.0`; pip, pipx and gem take
# abbreviations). The guard was fixed (a4bad97) and the class went with it.
